newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-BankItaly cut seen just round next corner.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-BankItaly cut seen just round next corner.

text.p: A strong performance by French Socialists in the first round of elections is unlikely to put the Bank of Italy off lowering interest rates soon, analysts say, although the timing of such a cut is, as ever, uncertain.
Expectation persists Italy's central bank is on the point of easing monetary policy, given falling inflation and high real interest rates, slow demand and crawling economic growth.

Markets have believed for weeks that a cut in the official 6.75 percent discount rate was always just round the corner and the lira's muted reaction to the left's strong showing in France has removed one factor analysts thought could delay an easing.
"It's now time for the Bank of Italy to cut the discount rate and the latest we can expect it to move is by the end of next week," said Pio De Gregorio at NatWest Markets here.
Many in the financial markets had expected the central bank would wait to see how the French vote went and its effect on the lira and bond markets. The second round runoff is next Sunday.

Apart from the final French vote, some analysts see the Bank of Italy holding off to see details of the government's three-year economic target document (DPEF), due to go before a cabinet meeting on Friday.

London and U.S. markets were closed on Monday but the lira was quoted at 985.80 per mark - firmer than its exchange rate mechanism central parity of 990 per mark and steady on Friday's levels. The cash bond market was weak but not dramatically so, holding 70-80 basis points off alongside weak Spanish Bonos.
"The market's view is even if the Socialists get a majority in the National Assembly the underlying politics of France on EMU will remain basically unchanged," De Gregorio said.
So what is the Bank of Italy waiting for?

Paolo Casadio at Credito Italiano noted Italy had falling inflation now 1.5 percent year on year and a public deficit at three percent of gross domestic product, in line with a key economic and monetary union (EMU) criterion and down from 6.7 percent last year.
"The exchange rate in the last few months has appreciated and seems fairly stable. Finally Italian industry is recovering. There has never been a better period than this," he said.

Casadio said all parts of society had worked to bring Italy's economy to order for EMU, with industrial margins down, unions agreeing low wage deals and a government working to reduce the budget deficit further.
As a result, he said: "I expect a rate cut Friday evening before the Bank of Italy annual report (on Saturday), with the markets closed, of 50 basis points."
Central bank governor Antonio Fazio will give his annual speech on Saturday morning.
Giuseppe Abbotto at Indosuez said the central bank might be waiting to see the contents of DPEF plan for 1998-2000.
The Italian press expect the DPEF will be accompanied by broad outlines of expected structural spending cuts and a sketch of the government's 1998 budget.

"You could say the bank is keeping up the pressure on the government by waiting for the presentation of the DPEF because it's waiting for signals (on structural spending cuts)," Abbotto said, adding he expected a 75 basis point easing.
Riccardo Antoniol at Bank of America also expected a 75 basis points easing by Saturday, based on domestic factors.
"I'm inclined to believe the Bank is waiting for the DPEF and its contents and the 1998 budget's measures on value-added tax changes and Italian public finances," he said.
"If this is the policy, they'll wait until the end of the week," he added.
